import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter

# Load the dataset from the string
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Visualization ---

# Set a visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the bubble chart
# X-axis: Price
# Y-axis: Megapixels
# Bubble Size: Weight
# Bubble Color: Sensor Type
# Marker Style: 4K Video Capability
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(200, 2500),  # Control min/max bubble size for clarity
    hue='sensor_type',
    style='has_video_4k',
    palette='plasma',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5
)

# --- Annotations and Customizations ---

# Add text labels for each point for more context
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    plt.text(
        x=df['price_usd'][i] + 50,
        y=df['megapixels'][i] + 0.5,
        s=f"{df['brand'][i]}\n({df['model_year'][i]})",
        fontdict=dict(color='black', size=10)
    )

# Improve title and labels
plt.title('Camera Feature Comparison: Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=20, pad=20, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
plt.ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the x-axis to show dollar signs and commas
formatter = FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f'${x:,.0f}')
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center')

# Adjust legend
# Move the legend outside the plot area
h, l = scatter.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually set legend titles for clarity
legend_titles = ['Sensor Type', 'Has 4K Video', 'Weight (grams)']
split_point = len(df['sensor_type'].unique()) + 1 # Split after hue
split_point2 = split_point + len(df['has_video_4k'].unique()) + 1 # Split after style

# Create separate legends
legend1 = plt.legend(h[:split_point], l[:split_point], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', title=legend_titles[0], title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')
ax = plt.gca().add_artist(legend1)
legend2 = plt.legend(h[split_point:split_point2], l[split_point:split_point2], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.75), loc='upper left', title=legend_titles[1], title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')
ax = plt.gca().add_artist(legend2)
legend3 = plt.legend(h[split_point2:], l[split_point2:], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.55), loc='upper left', title=legend_titles[2], title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')


# Final layout adjustments and save
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust layout to make room for legend
plt.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
